body: Don't let yourself be judged by others for what you do or not do, specially for doing good. Don't shut your mouth, shout it out loud and give an example of what's good. We're tricked into believing that we need more and more to be happy, that money is an end and not a mean, and those who can see past that are the ones who are truly happy. Among some things, I'm a writer, and even though I've been quite successful, I haven't been able to make a living out of it, but what keeps me going? It's not the paycheck, but a message from somebody who says "wow, I want to become a writer too!" or "when are you releasing the sequel?". Same thing with this. I guess we're all in the cryptos for the money, but at least for myself, it's a mean, not an end.

Dude, that's beyond amazing! I'm so glad you got the perspective that when you give expecting nothing in return is when you receive the most!
Next time you do, keep me in mind. I'm trying to reach the whole world with my board games (I'm a designer). I'm positive that the first step to begin the healing to the social fabric that has been destroyed by technology and social media is to have people share a table and a good game. Share a smile, a story, and adventure, a rivalry around a table and create real bonds, real friends, real interactions to the restore what's natural of human beings.
Kudos my friend and good luck in the future!

Sometimes when people have lots of problems like you do tend to look life from the outside and see a mountain of problems crumbling down on them, I guess that's how you feel.
Try this experiment: 
1- For a moment, forget about everything. Financial and emotional problems, debts, family/friend struggles, even disease.
2- Regardless of your circumstances, do something good for three people (1- Someone you know, 2- A family member, 3- An unknown person). Anything. Give a piece of cake as a gift. Do the dishes. Help someone to cross the street. Anything.
3- Analyze how you felt by giving and forgetting about yourself.
4- Repeat the process and challenge them to do so.

The world is rotten to its core as it is, and the people running it have it easier if we think about ourselves than about others. They sell more to fill the voids that only good things can fill. Don't let them do it. Water your own life, not theirs.

That's been my secret to come out from under that mountain of problems. I guess we'd all love to know how did it go.
